children: BTCUSD order book shows ~$37M of sell orders stacked at $85,122–$87,000 (resistance) and ~$21.1M of buy orders at $82,000–$83,500 (support); Spot ETF saw ~$2.6B weekly inflows.
BTCUSD saw extreme volatility near $84,000 in 24 hours; about 79,553 traders liquidated, totaling roughly $278.6 million in closed leveraged positions.
BTCUSD saw an early bull signal Aug 20 when adjusted MVRV 30‑day MA crossed above 365‑day MA near $71,255; over 31 days BTC rose ~13% to about $84,156, MVRV ~1.018.
Since Aug. 19, spot Bitcoin ETF inflows totaled about $4.6 billion, with year-to-date flows still positive—signaling ongoing institutional demand for BTCUSD exposure via regulated spot ETFs.
81% of circulating Bitcoin hasn't moved in over six months, shrinking effective BTCUSD spot float and raising risk of sharper moves if dormant supply starts trading; BVIV and bond volatility are low.
BTCUSD broke above its May high on the weekly chart, breaching the four-year cycle pattern. A weekly close above May confirms strength; a return below risks a false breakout and year-end correction.
A buyer resumed BTCUSD spot CFD purchases, acquiring 950 BTC (~$75.7M) at an average price of $79,670 — the first Bitcoin buy since late August.
In 96 hours whales bought ~30,269 BTC (~$2.57B) while BTCUSD traded near $84,580, below $86,853 high; price held above the 20‑day EMA amid lower long-term yields, ETF demand and bearish liquidations.
BTCUSD spot: near-term resistance ~84,000; longer-term resistance ~85,900–86,000; mean MVRV resistance ~96,700. 84,000 is key short-term reference for spot moves.
BTCUSD up ~50% from June 2026 lows; year-to-date spot CFD volume down ~30%, showing price rise alongside lower trading activity.
